subject: maths
title: Year 4 Equivalent Fractions
seo_title: Year 4 Equivalent Fractions Worksheets: Fraction Walls, Number Lines and Decimals (Free, with Answer Key)
standard_text: Find equivalent representations of fractions using related denominators and make connections between fractions and decimal notation
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on equivalent fractions for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4N03): shaded shapes, fraction walls, missing numerators and denominators, number lines, tenths, hundredths and decimals, and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Equivalent fractions: multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number.
key_sub: 3/4 = 6/8, because 3 × 2 = 6 and 4 × 2 = 8. Never add the same number to both: 2/3 is not 4/5. To write a decimal, make tenths or hundredths first: 3/5 = 6/10 = 0.6.
body_html:
What are equivalent fractions?

Equivalent fractions are worth the same amount, but use different numbers. A fraction wall shows them: look straight down to see which fractions line up.

Multiply or divide both numbers

To find an equivalent fraction, multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number. Use related denominators: halves, quarters and eighths; thirds, sixths and twelfths; fifths, tenths and hundredths.

Example

23 = ?12

3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the numerator by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8.

Answer: 8

Example

68 = ?4

8 ÷ 2 = 4, so divide the numerator by 2 too: 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

Answer: 3

On a number line

Equivalent fractions sit at the same point on number lines of the same length.

Fractions and decimals

Change the fraction to tenths or hundredths, then write it as a decimal. Tenths have one digit after the decimal point. Hundredths have two.

Example

Write 35 as a decimal.

5 × 2 = 10, so 35 = 610. 6 tenths = 0.6.

Answer: 0.6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the same number to the top and the bottom: 23 = 45Multiply both by the same number: 23 = 46
Changing only one part: 34 = 38Change both numbers: 34 = 68
Writing the digits as a decimal: 35 = 0.35Make tenths first: 35 = 610 = 0.6
Mixing up tenths and hundredths: 6100 = 0.66100 = 0.06, but 610 = 0.6

faq.q: What do Year 4 students learn about equivalent fractions?
faq.a: In the Australian Curriculum (AC9M4N03), Year 4 students find equivalent fractions with related denominators, such as 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8 and 1/3 = 2/6 = 4/12. They also connect fractions to decimals, for example 3/5 = 6/10 = 0.6.

faq.q: How do you find an equivalent fraction?
faq.a: Multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator by the same number. For 3/4 = ?/8, 4 × 2 = 8, so 3 × 2 = 6 and 3/4 = 6/8. Never add the same number to both.

faq.q: How do you change a fraction into a decimal in Year 4?
faq.a: Make an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 10 or 100, then write it as tenths or hundredths. For example, 3/5 = 6/10 = 0.6 and 1/4 = 25/100 = 0.25.
No. NAPLAN is for Years 3, 5, 7 and 9. Equivalent fractions and decimals in Year 4 build the skills students need for the Year 5 NAPLAN numeracy test.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 12 is shaded. How many eighths are equal to 12?
items.e: Look straight down the fraction wall. Each half is the same as 4 eighths, so 1 half lines up with 1 × 4 = 4 eighths. So 12 = 48.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 23 is shaded. How many twelfths are equal to 23?
items.e: Look straight down the fraction wall. Each third is the same as 4 twelfths, so 2 thirds line up with 2 × 4 = 8 twelfths. So 23 = 812.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 35 is shaded. How many tenths are equal to 35?
items.e: Look straight down the fraction wall. Each fifth is the same as 2 tenths, so 3 fifths line up with 3 × 2 = 6 tenths. So 35 = 610.

items.q: Use the fraction wall. 13 is shaded. How many sixths are equal to 13?
items.e: Look straight down the fraction wall. Each third is the same as 2 sixths, so 1 third lines up with 1 × 2 = 2 sixths. So 13 = 26.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Compare the shaded parts.
items.e: Both bars are shaded up to the same place. The bottom bar has more parts, but each part is smaller. So they are equal: 23 = 46.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Compare the shaded parts.
items.e: 34 is the same as 68. The bottom bar has 5 parts shaded, so the top bar has more: 34 > 58. More parts does not mean more shaded.

items.q: The bars are the same size. Compare the shaded parts.
items.e: 12 is the same as 48. The bottom bar has 5 parts shaded, so the bottom bar has more: 12 < 58. More parts does not mean more shaded.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to the shaded part?
items.e: 312 is shaded. 12 ÷ 3 = 4, so make groups of 3 parts: there are 4 groups and 1 is shaded. 312 = 14. 912 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to the shaded part?
items.e: 410 is shaded. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: 410 = 25. 45 only changes the denominator, and 210 only changes the numerator.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to the shaded part?
items.e: 28 is shaded. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: 28 = 14. 68 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: 68 = ?4

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 23?
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the numerator by 4 too: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 = 812. 45 adds 2 to both numbers, 26 changes only the denominator and 83 changes only the numerator.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 45?
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, so multiply the numerator by 2 too: 4 × 2 = 8. So 45 = 810. 67 adds 2 to both numbers. Adding changes the value.

items.q: Which fraction is not equal to 12?
items.e: 34 is not equal to 12: 2 was added to the numerator and the denominator. Adding changes the value. The others are equal, because both numbers were multiplied by the same number (× 2, × 4, × 5).

items.q: Which fraction is not equal to 34?
items.e: 56 is not equal to 34: 2 was added to the numerator and the denominator. Adding changes the value. The others are equal, because both numbers were multiplied by the same number (× 2, × 3, × 25).

items.q: The number lines are the same length. The arrow shows 12. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line has 6 equal parts. Follow the dashed line down and count the marks from 0: 3. So 12 = 36 (1 × 3 = 3 and 2 × 3 = 6).

items.q: The number lines are the same length. The arrow shows 13. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line has 6 equal parts. Follow the dashed line down and count the marks from 0: 2. So 13 = 26 (1 × 2 = 2 and 3 × 2 = 6).

items.q: The number lines are the same length. The arrow shows 34. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line has 8 equal parts. Follow the dashed line down and count the marks from 0: 6. So 34 = 68 (3 × 2 = 6 and 4 × 2 = 8).

items.q: The number lines are the same length. The arrow shows 23. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line has 6 equal parts. Follow the dashed line down and count the marks from 0: 4. So 23 = 46 (2 × 2 = 4 and 3 × 2 = 6).

items.q: The number lines are the same length. The arrow shows 12. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line has 10 equal parts. Follow the dashed line down and count the marks from 0: 5. So 12 = 510 (1 × 5 = 5 and 2 × 5 = 10).

items.q: The number lines are the same length. The arrow shows 45. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line has 10 equal parts. Follow the dashed line down and count the marks from 0: 8. So 45 = 810 (4 × 2 = 8 and 5 × 2 = 10).

items.q: The number lines are the same length. The arrow shows 56. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line has 12 equal parts. Follow the dashed line down and count the marks from 0: 10. So 56 = 1012 (5 × 2 = 10 and 6 × 2 = 12).

items.q: The number lines are the same length. The arrow shows 14. Which fraction on the bottom line is at the same point?
items.e: The bottom line has 8 equal parts. Follow the dashed line down and count the marks from 0: 2. So 14 = 28 (1 × 2 = 2 and 4 × 2 = 8).

items.q: Which letter shows 34?
items.e: The line is split into 8 equal parts, so each mark is 18. 34 = 68 (multiply both numbers by 2). Count 6 marks from 0: that is letter C.

items.q: Which letter shows 12?
items.e: The line is split into 8 equal parts, so each mark is 18. 12 = 48 (multiply both numbers by 4). Count 4 marks from 0: that is letter A.

items.q: Which letter shows 23?
items.e: The line is split into 6 equal parts, so each mark is 16. 23 = 46 (multiply both numbers by 2). Count 4 marks from 0: that is letter D.

items.q: Which letter shows 35?
items.e: The line is split into 10 equal parts, so each mark is 110. 35 = 610 (multiply both numbers by 2). Count 6 marks from 0: that is letter B.

items.q: Which letter shows 14?
items.e: The line is split into 8 equal parts, so each mark is 18. 14 = 28 (multiply both numbers by 2). Count 2 marks from 0: that is letter A.

items.q: Which letter shows 56?
items.e: The line is split into 12 equal parts, so each mark is 112. 56 = 1012 (multiply both numbers by 2). Count 10 marks from 0: that is letter D.

items.q: The arrow points to 68. Which fraction is at the same point?
items.e: The line has 8 equal parts and the arrow is 6 marks from 0. Group the marks in 2s: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 groups, so the line is also split into quarters. 6 ÷ 2 = 3, so 68 = 34.

items.q: The arrow points to 812. Which fraction is at the same point?
items.e: The line has 12 equal parts and the arrow is 8 marks from 0. Group the marks in 4s: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 groups, so the line is also split into thirds. 8 ÷ 4 = 2, so 812 = 23.

items.q: The arrow points to 28. Which fraction is at the same point?
items.e: The line has 8 equal parts and the arrow is 2 marks from 0. Group the marks in 2s: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 groups, so the line is also split into quarters. 2 ÷ 2 = 1, so 28 = 14.

items.q: The arrow points to 810. Which fraction is at the same point?
items.e: The line has 10 equal parts and the arrow is 8 marks from 0. Group the marks in 2s: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 groups, so the line is also split into fifths. 8 ÷ 2 = 4, so 810 = 45.

items.q: The arrow points to 1012. Which fraction is at the same point?
items.e: The line has 12 equal parts and the arrow is 10 marks from 0. Group the marks in 2s: 12 ÷ 2 = 6 groups, so the line is also split into sixths. 10 ÷ 2 = 5, so 1012 = 56.

items.q: The arrow points to 410. Which fraction is at the same point?
items.e: The line has 10 equal parts and the arrow is 4 marks from 0. Group the marks in 2s: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 groups, so the line is also split into fifths. 4 ÷ 2 = 2, so 410 = 25.

sets.title: Fractions as decimals: tenths and hundredths

items.q: 35 = 610 = ?
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, so 35 = 610. 6 tenths is written 0.6. Do not just write the digits 3 and 5 as a decimal.

items.q: 15 = 210 = ?
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, so 15 = 210. 2 tenths is written 0.2. Do not just write the digits 1 and 5 as a decimal.

items.q: Write 45 as a decimal.
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, so 45 = 810. 8 tenths is written 0.8. Do not just write the digits 4 and 5 as a decimal.

items.q: Write 25 as a decimal.
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, so 25 = 410. 4 tenths is written 0.4. Do not just write the digits 2 and 5 as a decimal.

items.q: 12 = 510 = ?
items.e: 2 × 5 = 10, so 12 = 510. 5 tenths is written 0.5. 0.12 and 1.2 just join the digits 1 and 2.

items.q: 710 = ?100
items.e: 10 × 10 = 100, so multiply the numerator by 10 too: 7 × 10 = 70. So 710 = 70100. Both are 0.7.

items.q: 0.9 = ?100
items.e: 0.9 is 9 tenths, 910. 10 × 10 = 100, so 9 × 10 = 90. So 0.9 = 910 = 90100.

items.q: 14 = 25100 = ?
items.e: 25100 is 25 hundredths, written 0.25. 0.14 and 1.4 just join the digits, and 0.4 is 4 tenths.

items.q: 34 = ?100
items.e: 4 × 25 = 100, so multiply the numerator by 25 too: 3 × 25 = 75. So 34 = 75100 = 0.75. 25 is the part that is left.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.4?
items.e: 0.4 is 4 tenths, 410. Divide the numerator and the denominator by 2: 410 = 25. 4100 is 0.04, and 14 is 0.25.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.75?
items.e: 0.75 is 75 hundredths, 75100. 100 ÷ 25 = 4 and 75 ÷ 25 = 3, so 75100 = 34. 14 is 0.25, the part that is left.

items.q: 0.8 = ?5
items.e: 0.8 is 8 tenths, 810. 10 ÷ 2 = 5, so divide the numerator by 2 too: 8 ÷ 2 = 4. So 0.8 = 45.

items.q: The grid has 100 equal squares. Which decimal shows the shaded part?
items.e: 60 of 100 squares are shaded: 60100 = 610. 6 tenths is 0.6. 0.4 is the part that is not shaded.

items.q: The grid has 100 equal squares. Which decimal shows the shaded part?
items.e: 25 of 100 squares are shaded: 25100, which is written 0.25. It is also 14.

items.q: Which of these is not equal to the shaded part?
items.e: 30 of 100 squares are shaded: 30100 = 310 = 0.3. 3100 would be only 3 squares.

items.q: Which of these is not equal to 0.5?
items.e: 0.5 = 510 = 50100 = 12. 15 = 210 = 0.2, so it is not equal to 0.5.

items.q: Which of these is not equal to 35?
items.e: 35 = 610 = 60100 = 0.6. 0.35 just joins the digits 3 and 5, so it is not equal.

items.q: The line is split into tenths. Which decimal does the arrow show?
items.e: Each mark is 110 = 0.1. The arrow is 7 marks from 0, so it shows 710 = 0.7.

items.q: The line is split into fifths. Which decimal does the arrow show?
items.e: The arrow shows 45. 5 × 2 = 10, so 45 = 810 = 0.8. The line has fifths, not tenths, so 0.4 is wrong.

items.q: Which is greater: 35 or 0.5?
items.e: 35 = 610 = 0.6. 0.6 is more than 0.5, so 35 is greater.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Jack eats 34 of the pizza. How many slices does he eat?
items.e: 4 × 2 = 8, so 34 = 68. Jack eats 6 slices.

items.q: A tray holds 12 lamingtons. Oliver’s family eats 23 of the tray. How many lamingtons do they eat?
items.e: 3 × 4 = 12, so multiply the numerator by 4 too: 23 = 812. They eat 8 lamingtons.

items.q: A 2 L bottle of juice is poured equally into 10 cups. How much juice is in each cup?
items.e: Each cup gets 210 L. Divide both numbers by 2: 210 = 15 = 0.2 L.

items.q: Mia and Leo share a 2 L bottle of water. Mia drinks 0.5 L and Leo drinks 12 L. Who drinks more?
items.e: 12 = 510 = 0.5. So they drink the same amount.

items.q: A 2 L bottle of lemonade is shared equally by 4 friends. Each friend gets 24 L. Which is the same amount?
items.e: 24 = 12 = 510, which is 0.5 L. 0.24 and 2.4 just join the digits.

items.q: Noah says 23 = 45, because he added 2 to the top and the bottom. Is he right?
c: No. 23 = 46
No. 23 = 43
No. 23 = 26

items.e: Adding the same number changes the value. Multiply both numbers by 2 instead: 23 = 46.

items.q: Ruby says 34 = 38, because the numerators are the same. Is she right?
c: Yes. The numerators are the same
No. 34 = 68
No. 34 = 32
No. 34 = 78
items.e: Ruby changed only the denominator. Eighths are smaller than quarters, so she needs more of them. Multiply both numbers by 2: 34 = 68.

items.q: At footy training, Cooper runs 34 of a lap and Kai runs 68 of a lap. Who runs further?
items.e: Multiply both numbers in 34 by 2: 34 = 68. So they run the same distance.

items.q: At netball, Amelia scores 4 goals from 10 shots. Which fraction in fifths shows the shots she scored?
items.e: She scored 410 of her shots. Divide both numbers by 2: 410 = 25. 35 are the shots she missed.

items.q: In a Year 4 class, 610 of the students walk to school. Write this as a decimal.
items.e: 610 is 6 tenths, written 0.6. 0.4 is the students who do not walk.

items.q: Grace has a 1 m ribbon. She cuts off 0.25 m. What fraction of a metre does she cut off?
items.e: 0.25 m = 25100 m. 25 × 4 = 100, so 25100 = 14.

items.q: A block of chocolate has 12 equal pieces. Liam eats 13 of the block and Sienna eats 312. Who eats more?
items.e: 13 = 412, so Liam eats 4 pieces. Sienna eats 3 pieces. Liam eats more.

items.q: At the sausage sizzle, a tray holds 10 sausages. 45 of them are cooked. How many sausages are cooked?
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, so 45 = 810. 8 sausages are cooked.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, Charlotte has swum 50 m of a 100 m race. Which fraction of the race has she swum?
items.e: She has swum 50100 of the race. 50 × 2 = 100, so 50100 = 12.

items.q: A cake is cut into 6 equal pieces. Mum keeps 13 of the cake for tomorrow. How many pieces is that?
items.e: 3 × 2 = 6, so 13 = 26. That is 2 pieces.

items.q: Kai has 10 apples. 7 of them are green. Which decimal shows the part that is green?
items.e: 7 out of 10 is 710, which is written 0.7. 0.3 is the part that is not green.

items.q: How many cents is 34 of $1?
items.e: $1 is 100 cents. 4 × 25 = 100, so 34 = 75100. That is 75c.

items.q: The school vegetable garden has 100 equal squares. 30 squares have tomatoes. Mei says that is 0.3 of the garden. Is she right?
c: Yes. 30100 = 310 = 0.3
items.e: 30 of 100 squares is 30100. Divide both numbers by 10: 310 = 0.3. Yes, she is right.

items.q: Matilda eats 28 of a pizza. Aarav eats 14 of a pizza of the same size. Who eats more?
items.e: Divide both numbers in 28 by 2: 28 = 14. So they eat the same amount.

items.q: Three students run around the oval. Oliver runs 0.4 km, Ava runs 25 km and Jack runs 410 km. Who runs the furthest?
items.e: 25 = 410 = 0.4. All three distances are the same, so they all run the same.
